page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c4.2xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the KVM hypervisor and powered by an Intel Xeon 8369HB processor. It features 8 dedicated physical cores with 1 thread per core, operating at a clock speed of 3.2 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The CPU includes 32 KB L1d cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 33 MB L3 cache, with hardware support for AVX-512 and vector neural network instructions. The instance is configured with 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding a 2.0 GB per core ratio, and does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware. Network connectivity is supported by a baseline bandwidth of 3 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations place the ecs.c4.2xlarge in the average performance tier for most standard compute tasks. It achieves a stress-ng single-core score of 1575.79 and a multi-core score of 8310.78, alongside a Geekbench multi-core score of 4720.0. Memory performance is mixed; while cached small-block read bandwidth is measured at 464.83 GB/sec, large-block uncached read bandwidth drops to 37.74 GB/sec, which is reflected in a lower PassMark memory score of 1525.1. The instance performs adequately on static web serving at 7.7 GB/sec and Redis SET operations at 8.09 million operations per second, but exhibits poor performance on larger workloads, such as LLM inference with a 7B model, which yields 5.16 tokens per second for text generation.

Given its dedicated CPU allocation and 1:2 memory-to-vCPU ratio, the ecs.c4.2xlarge offers a cost-efficient profile for compute-bound workloads that do not require massive memory footprints or local storage. It is appropriate for tasks such as software compilation, lightweight web serving, and moderate computational tasks. However, the lack of local storage and weak performance in database operations and large-block memory reads make it less appropriate for memory-intensive databases or large-scale data processing.
